01 — Organization

What is Widows Sons?

An international fraternal riding association for Master Masons — men who are Freemasons first, and motorcyclists second.

The Association, worldwide

The Widows Sons Masonic Riders Association (Widows Sons MRA) is an international fraternity of motorcycle-riding Freemasons, founded by Carl A. Davenport. Membership is open exclusively to Master Masons (Third Degree) in good standing with a regularly recognized Grand Lodge. Chapters ride together, support one another, and carry out charitable work — with particular care for the widows of Master Masons and their families, in keeping with the association's name.

Chapter Hellas

Widows Sons MRA Chapter Hellas is the Greek chapter of the association. It currently operates under the aegis of, and in consultation with, the Widows Sons MRA Grand Chapter Bulgaria and/or the Widows Sons Illinois Presidents Council, pending the eventual formation — once the relevant conditions are met — of an independent Chapter of Greece, at which point the Chapter would fall directly under the international Widows Sons MRA organization. Chapter Hellas may propose new sub-chapters within Greek territory to its Chapter Committee.

Purpose

Chapter Hellas exists to protect and support its members and their families, and to assist the widows of Master Masons whenever the need arises. Members are encouraged to remain in good standing with their Lodge, to conduct themselves properly, and to take part in lawful activities that reflect well on Freemasonry. The Chapter undertakes at least one annual charitable donation, and a donation is made a matter of course at every regular meeting toward a cause of the Chapter's choosing. The organization takes no part in political, religious, or divisive activity, and no member may wear the insignia of a "1%" club while wearing the Widows Sons patch.

Membership

Widows Sons runs on Motorcycle Club custom. The Chapter is composed of Master Masons — Third Degree — recognized by the Grand Lodge of Greece (Μεγάλη Στοά της Ελλάδος) or another regularly recognized Grand Lodge who present a Certificate of Good Standing. A brother who has not yet reached the Third Degree rides as a prospect: welcome in the Chapter, but not yet entitled to wear the full patch. Every candidate serves a minimum six-month petition period before being proposed for the Center Patch, followed by a further one-year probation before becoming eligible for full colors. Sponsors must present a candidate's case thirty days before any vote, and the award of the Center Patch requires a unanimous vote of those present.

Alongside full membership, an associated outreach initiative — Masonic Riders Hellas — welcomes recognized brethren who do not yet meet the requirements for full membership but share the association's values, so that they may take part in nearly all of the Chapter's activities without distinction.

The partners of members are known as Widows Sons Ladies. They are not Freemasons, and they do not join Widows Sons or wear its patches — but they're very welcome to ride and take part in the Chapter's social activities. Rituals and Widows Sons meetings remain for members only.

  • Full Patch Member: a Master Mason (3°) in good standing who has completed petition and probation; wears the complete Widows Sons patch set.
  • Prospect: a 1° or 2° brother; rides and takes part in Chapter life, but does not wear the full patch.
  • Widows Sons Lady: the partner of a member; not a Freemason, and does not wear Widows Sons insignia.
  • Rituals & meetings: open to members only; Ladies join the rides and social side of Chapter life.

02 — Administration

Officers of the Chapter / Αξιωματικοί του Chapter

The Chapter is administered by 15 officers. The first six are the Principal Officers — Κύριοι Αξιωματικοί. The Founding President — Ιδρυτικός Πρόεδρος και Οικιστής is a permanent special founding distinction and is not counted as a separate office.

The President, Treasurer and Road Captain serve five-year terms. The remaining appointments are made in accordance with the Chapter rules and decisions of the President.

Offices defined by the Constitution — Article 5

The Chapter's Constitution provides for four elected representatives — President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer — elected annually in that order, plus a full slate of appointed officers who serve the Chapter's operations and are named by the President within thirty days of taking office:

Sergeant-at-Arms Road Captain Ambassador Warden Orator Almoner Guard Quartermaster Master of Ceremonies Steward Assistant Event Manager

03 — Emblem

The Chapter Hellas Emblem

Every element of the patch carries meaning — worn only by members in good standing, and always remaining the property of Widows Sons MRA.

  • Top Rocker
    "Masonic Riders Assn." — identifies the wearer as a member of the worldwide Masonic Riders Association.
  • Widows Sons
    The association's name in red script across the crown of the emblem, above the winged triangle.
  • Winged Triangle
    A triangle bearing the square and the All-Seeing Eye, flanked by outstretched wings — the eye watches over the Brotherhood, the wings carry its charity outward.
  • Twin Columns
    Two pillars set at the base of the triangle, echoing the pillars of the Craft Lodge.
  • Motto
    "Meet on the Level & Part upon the Square" — arcs beneath the triangle in red script.
  • Bottom Rocker
    "Chapter Hellas" — the Greek chapter's designation, worn beneath the central patch.
Rights to the Widows Sons name, emblem and insignia belong exclusively to Widows Sons MRA. Members hold their patches only for as long as they remain in good standing, and all insignia are returned to the Chapter upon a member's departure (Article 10).
Καταστατικό
04 — Constitution

Constitution of Chapter Hellas

Articles 1–4 establish who the Chapter is, why it exists, and who may belong to it.

I

Name

Establishes the organization as Widows Sons Masonic Riders Association — Chapter Hellas, represented by a non-profit legal association, operating as an independent Chapter in Greece.

II

Purpose

Protection and welfare of members and their families, aid to widows, at least one annual charitable donation, and strict neutrality on political and religious matters.

III

Members

Master Masons in good standing with the National Grand Lodge of Greece or another recognized Grand Lodge; petition, Center Patch, and full-colors probation periods; the Masonic Riders Hellas outreach initiative; honorary membership for sitting and past Grand Masters.

IV

Withdrawal & Reserve Status

Provides for temporary reserve status on grounds of advanced age or medical necessity, with voting rights and full reinstatement decided by member vote.

Κανονισμοί
05 — By-Laws

Regulations & Operating Rules

Articles 5–13 govern how the Chapter is run day to day: officers, elections, meetings, motorcycles, finances and discipline.

The Chapter's Constitution and By-Laws, and the Mother Chapter's and sister chapter's reference by-laws, kept as they should be — bound, shelved, and watched over.

V

Officers

Defines the full slate of Chapter offices and the duties of each — President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, Sergeant-at-Arms, Road Captain, Almoner, Warden, Orator, Ambassador, Master of Ceremonies and Quartermaster.

VI

Elections

The President and the Treasurer are elected for a five-year term. All other officers — the Vice President, Secretary, and the other Sergeants — are appointed by the President for a one-year term, which the President may extend at his own discretion and order.

VII

Meetings

Monthly regular meetings conducted under Robert's Rules of Order; attendance requirements for members and officers; a two-thirds majority for decisions.

VIII

Motorcycles

Minimum engine displacement, a valid roadworthiness certificate (ΚΤΕΟ), liability insurance and a Category A motorcycle license for every member.

IX

Funerals

A standing three-member Funeral Committee attends the funeral of any member or close relative, wearing the Widows Sons emblem in tribute.

X

Logos & Insignia

Ownership and stewardship of patches, the required top rocker and shoulder emblem, and the rule that insignia may only be worn on the Chapter's approved black leather vest.

XI

Finances

Initial membership fee covering colors and regalia, annual dues plus a charitable contribution, and honorary members' exemption from mandatory fees.

XII

Mandatory Events

One mandatory annual event or ride approved by unanimous vote, plus dedicated fundraising events for the Chapter's chosen charitable cause.

XIII

Grievances & Disputes

The Round Table — President, Vice President, Secretary and Officers — hears complaints and disputes between members, officers or chapters, with written charges and a formal hearing.

06 — Dress Code

Vest & Patch Regulations

All insignia are sewn onto an approved black leather vest, positioned according to the Chapter's official patch layout.

PatchSize (W × H)PositionFrom ShoulderFrom Center Line
Greek Flag15 × 6 cmUpper left chest11 cm12 cm (left)
Office / Rank15 × 5 cmLeft chest — middle19 cm12 cm (left)
Road Name15 × 5 cmLeft chest — lower25 cm12 cm (left)
Honorary15 × 5 cmLeft chest — below Road Name31 cm12 cm (left)
Chapter Hellas Emblem15 × 10 cmUpper right chest10 cm12 cm (right)
Founder15 × 5 cmRight chest — lower25 cm12 cm (right)
  • Insignia are sewn onto an approved black leather vest — no other garment is authorized to carry them.
  • The "Masonic Riders Assn." top rocker is worn above the central back patch on the vest or jacket.
  • The Masonic emblem must be visible on the left shoulder of every Widows Sons vest.
  • Black background with white border and lettering throughout, except red script within the official emblem.
  • The official Chapter Hellas emblem is used exactly as issued — no alteration is permitted.
  • All insignia remain the property of Widows Sons MRA and are returned to the Chapter upon a member's departure.
